title: Prompt Injection: Can a Document Hijack Your AI?
reader_task: Understand how text inside a document can attempt to redirect an AI (indirect prompt injection), why conversion does not establish trust, and which review and permission limits reduce risk. Education only.
scope_exclusions: Conflicting legitimate document versions belong to M12
Recognizing untrusted instructions, format-versus-trust demonstration and action authorization in depth belong to M11-S1, S2, S3
No live attacks, secret extraction or testing against real accounts or models
No claim that LLMiser detects, labels or removes injected instructions
description: Document prompt injection explained: how text hidden in a file can try to redirect an AI, why conversion doesn't make it safe, and which checks and limits help.
description_change: Rewritten to explain the risk and limits; contains the primary keyword; 159 characters.
excerpt: We hid one harmless instruction in a Word file, a web page and a slide deck. Conversion didn't remove it. It made it visible, and that turned out to be useful.
author: DevBehindYou
